rubric.why: Photolysis is the light-driven splitting of water during photosynthesis.
rubric.description: States that light energy splits water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying light-driven splitting of water.

rubric.why: The products of water splitting include oxygen and hydrogen-related particles.
rubric.description: Names the products released by photolysis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for oxygen and hydrogen ions/electrons, or an equivalent description.

modelAnswer: Photolysis is the splitting of water molecules by light energy during photosynthesis.
It releases oxygen, hydrogen ions and electrons.

items.followUp: What is meant by a source in the translocation of food in plants?

rubric.why: A sink is a plant location that receives translocated food.
rubric.description: Identifies a sink as a part or region of a plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a plant part or region.

rubric.why: Sinks use or store the food transported from sources.
rubric.description: States that the food is used or stored there.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning use or storage of food.

modelAnswer: A sink is a part of a plant where transported food is used or stored.

items.followUp: State two structural features of white blood cells.

rubric.why: Red blood cells have a characteristic biconcave disc shape.
rubric.description: States the shape of a red blood cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its biconcave disc shape.

rubric.why: Mature red blood cells lack a nucleus and contain haemoglobin.
rubric.description: Gives a key structural feature besides shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mature cells lack a nucleus or contain haemoglobin.

modelAnswer: Red blood cells are small, flexible, biconcave discs.
In humans, mature red blood cells have no nucleus and contain haemoglobin.

items.followUp: What is meant by transplantation surgery?

rubric.why: Vascular surgery specifically involves operations on blood vessels.
rubric.description: Identifies the operation as involving blood vessels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking surgery or operations with blood vessels.

rubric.why: The procedures treat vessel disorders or restore blood flow.
rubric.description: States the purpose of vascular surgery.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant purpose, such as treating vessel disease, repairing vessels or restoring blood flow.

modelAnswer: Vascular surgery is surgery performed on blood vessels, such as arteries and veins.
It is used to treat their disorders or restore normal blood flow.

items.followUp: Describe how Biology is related to Biochemistry and Bioinformatics.

rubric.why: Biophysics applies ideas and methods from physics to biological systems and processes.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship of Biology to Biophysics.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for stating that physics principles or methods are applied to the study of living organisms or their processes.

rubric.why: Biomathematics applies mathematical and statistical methods to biological questions and data.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship of Biology to Biomathematics.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for explaining that mathematical or statistical methods are used to study biological problems or data.

rubric.why: An example demonstrates how these related fields help investigate biological questions.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant example or application.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable application, such as modelling population growth or analysing biological data.

modelAnswer: Biophysics is the application of the principles and methods of physics to the study of living organisms and their processes.
It helps explain biological phenomena using physical laws and techniques.
Biomathematics applies mathematical and statistical methods to biological problems and data.
For example, mathematical models can be used to study population growth.
Thus, both fields use other disciplines to investigate biological questions.

items.followUp: Compare the functions of skeletal and cardiac muscles.

rubric.why: Skeletal muscle is striated and usually under voluntary control.
rubric.description: Describes skeletal muscle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying skeletal muscle as striated and voluntary.

rubric.why: Smooth muscle is non-striated and involuntary.
rubric.description: Describes smooth muscle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying smooth muscle as unstriated and involuntary.

rubric.why: Cardiac muscle is found in the heart and acts involuntarily.
rubric.description: Describes cardiac muscle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying cardiac muscle as heart muscle that is involuntary.

rubric.why: Location or a distinguishing structural feature adds a valid comparison of the tissue types.
rubric.description: Gives a distinguishing location or feature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct feature or location, such as skeletal muscles attached to bones, smooth muscles in internal organs, or branched cardiac fibres.

modelAnswer: Skeletal (striated) muscle has long fibres, is usually attached to bones and works voluntarily.
Smooth (unstriated) muscle has spindle-shaped cells, occurs in the walls of internal organs and works involuntarily.
Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart; its branched, striated fibres contract involuntarily.
Thus, the three muscle tissues differ in structure, location and control.

items.followUp: Describe two uses of enzymes in industry or medicine.

rubric.why: Enzymes are used in food production and processing.
rubric.description: Gives a food-industry use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example, such as cheese-making, bread-making or food processing.

rubric.why: Enzymes in detergents break down protein, fat or other stains.
rubric.description: Gives a detergent use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that enzymes help detergents remove stains.

rubric.why: Enzymes have important applications in medical diagnosis and treatment.
rubric.description: Gives a medical use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid diagnostic or therapeutic use.

rubric.why: Enzymes are used to process materials in several industries.
rubric.description: Gives another industrial use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid industrial example, such as leather, textile or paper processing.

rubric.why: Their catalytic action underlies their practical uses.
rubric.description: States the relevant action of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that enzymes act as biological catalysts or break down substances in these applications.

modelAnswer: Enzymes act as biological catalysts and are used in many fields.
In the food industry, they are used in processes such as cheese-making and bread-making.
Enzymes in detergents break down stains and help clean clothes.
In medicine, enzymes are used in diagnostic tests and some treatments.
They are also used in industries such as leather, textile and paper processing.

items.followUp: Name one product obtained through agriculture and state its importance.

rubric.why: Agriculture involves crop cultivation and/or the raising of useful animals.
rubric.description: Describes the work involved in agriculture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning crop cultivation or raising livestock.

rubric.why: Agriculture provides food and useful materials for people and industries.
rubric.description: States a product or importance of agriculture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming food, fibre, raw materials or another valid agricultural product.

modelAnswer: Agriculture is the profession and practice of cultivating crops and raising useful animals.
It supplies food and useful products such as fibres and other raw materials.
